text:
li: hey everyone  second day here. i created a hosted API key from Console to play with streaming, but my dev machine (on corp wifi) drops the stream after ~10s. non-stream requests work. should i switch to sandbox for prototyping or is there a config i missed?

nina: welcome li! :wave: corp proxies often kill long-lived websockets. sandbox is fine for quick prototyping because its endpoint uses chunked HTTPS which survives many proxies. hosted keys are fine but need proxy allowlisting for websocket traffic.

charlie: short checklist i use: 1) try non-streaming chunked endpoint first, 2) set HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY if your env requires it, 3) add our gateway CA to system trust store if you see TLS handshake errors, 4) use REDWOOD_API_URL to point to sandbox while developing.

li: how do i tell if i'm hitting a quota vs the proxy cutting the stream?

nina: watch response headers for non-stream calls. we expose X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-Quota-Bucket. if you get a 429 you'll also see Retry-After. Proxy drops will look like connection resets or 502/504 without rate headers.

charlie: quick curl to inspect headers:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -d '{"input":"test"}' https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate
```
Look for lines like `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0` or `X-Quota-Bucket: sandbox-42`.

li: thanks. i'm also using GH Actions for some smoke tests. is it OK to use a web-issued sandbox key there?

nina: don't use web-issued personal sandbox keys in CI. Create a service account key and store it in your secrets manager. Service account keys can be scoped to sandbox or hosted pools depending on your needs.

charlie: for nightly CI bursts, prefer a service account mapped to a hosted dev pool or request a temporary quota bump for the service account. If you need a one-off demo with higher throughput, file a support ticket with the window and expected tokens/min.

li: who does the ticket go to and what info do they want?

help-bot: To request quota changes open #help or Console > Support. Include: account id, key/service-account id, desired tokens/min or requests/min, start/end time, and contact. Small dev bumps usually processed same day.

li: one last thing  how do we rotate/revoke keys after a demo?

charlie: delete the key in Console > API Keys or rotate via service account UI. For ephemeral dev tokens use the `redwood` CLI which mints short-lived tokens tied to your SSO; those expire automatically. For CI use service accounts so you can rotate without breaking personal envs.

li: awesome, i'll try sandbox for local streaming tests and create a service account for CI. thanks y'all! :pray:
